quarterly_data.signal: Second-line breast cancer (zovegalisib): Chief Corporate Development Officer Pete said Relay is 'preparing to become a commercial company' and moving toward registrational readouts in breast cancer and vascular anomalies. COO Imogen said ReDiscover-2 enrollment is going well and Relay expects to do very well against benchmarks for similarly sized studies, with a separate team standing up the frontline study. Pete: there is no stomatitis or rash to speak of in the second-line AE table, the grade 3 hyperglycemia rate remains in the low single digits across over 100 patients treated at this exposure, and no prophylactic concomitant therapies are needed. Imogen said capivasertib remains the bar to beat: gedatolisib showed an 11-month PFS in PIK3CA-mutated patients at ASCO, but she called its weekly IV dosing onerous versus an oral option.
quarterly_data.figure: grade 3 hyperglycemia in the low single digits across over 100 patients

quarterly_data.signal: First-line breast cancer: COO Imogen said the triplet data in a median third-line population showed an ORR of 44%. The planned Phase III in endocrine-sensitive patients largely emulates Pfizer's FourLight-3 study of atirmociclib; within the U.S. the FDA has been pretty clear Relay could reference FourLight-3, while ex-U.S. Relay is considering a small contribution-of-parts arm; the goal is to launch in the first half of next year, early part of 2027. She said the exposure DDI with atirmociclib is manageable and predictable and Relay is confident in its RP3D. Pete said the Phase I/II continues to enroll zovegalisib plus atirmociclib plus fulvestrant in second-line-plus patients, with smaller arms using an aromatase inhibitor and in endocrine-resistant patients, and that precedent shows response rates tend to improve by 20% to 30% when moving into the front-line population.
quarterly_data.figure: triplet ORR 44% (median third-line); Phase III launch targeted early part of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Vascular anomalies (Chief Corporate Development Officer Pete): in the handful of patients with 24-week scans, every patient in response saw a deepening of response; activity was similar across subsets, and enrollment is roughly 70%, 75% PROS and 25%, 30% lymphatic malformation patients with no difference in performance (some of the deepest responses in lymphatic malformation). At 100 milligrams BID efficacy was modestly better than alpelisib with dramatically better safety, and at 300 milligrams twice daily the response rate was 100%; dose finding has started in the 6 to 11 population (weight-based, targeting roughly 400 milligrams once daily exposure), with 2 to 5-year-olds to follow. The regulatory endpoint is volumetric response rate with exclusion of 15% in the lower bound of the confidence interval; Relay does not believe it would require that many patients and will ask the FDA about pooling and data-set size. He put the addressable population at about 15,000 U.S. patients with moderate severe disease within PROS and lymphatic malformations.
quarterly_data.figure: 100% response rate at 300 milligrams twice daily; about 15,000 U.S. addressable patients; endpoint excludes 15% at the lower bound
